prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3056 adds `_is_optional_str()` which only disables pre-parsing when the union's sole non-None member is `str` (i.e. exactly `Optional[str]`), leaving JSON pre-parsing behavior unchanged for every other union shape (e.g. `str | int`, `str | list[str]`) where decoding a numeric/list-shaped string still has a plausible use case. 2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` instead skips pre-parsing for ANY union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} — e.g. it also disables parsing for `str | int` and `str | bool` unions, which is a broader behavior change than the reported corruption bug (which only affects Optional[str]) and isn't covered by the PR's stated scope ('str union annotations') or justified in its diff. 3056's docstring also explicitly documents the reasoning (no member of Optional[str] besides str can result from decoding, so parsing can only corrupt, never help), making the narrower scope traceable to the actual bug.

clusters.pick_reason: 3056 adds `_is_optional_str()` which only disables pre-parsing when the union's sole non-None member is `str` (i.e. exactly `Optional[str]`), leaving JSON pre-parsing behavior unchanged for every other union shape (e.g. `str | int`, `str | list[str]`) where decoding a numeric/list-shaped string still has a plausible use case. 2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` instead skips pre-parsing for ANY union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} — e.g. it also disables parsing for `str | int` and `str | bool` unions, which is a broader behavior change than the reported corruption bug (which only affects Optional[str]) and isn't covered by the PR's stated scope ('str union annotations') or justified in its diff. 3056's docstring also explicitly documents the reasoning (no member of Optional[str] besides str can result from decoding, so parsing can only corrupt, never help), making the narrower scope traceable to the actual bug.
